It calls a cleanup routine at the end, and raises an alert and returns an error code when setup fails.

name: release_process_resources_and_reply
description: Stores its parameter as the return value, then closes a file handle, closes a library base and frees a memory block, each step guarded by a stored pointer. It finishes with a forbid-and-reply call through the library table and returns the saved parameter.

name: start_resident_tool_task
description: Opens the icon and intuition libraries and decodes a fixed string in place with a one-byte key. It then looks up the named resident tag and starts the tool, reporting a missing tag or a failed start with the error code.

name: compare_null_terminated_strings
description: Compares two null-terminated strings byte by byte. It returns a negative value when the first is less than the second, one when it is greater, and zero when they are equal.

name: build_lookup_node_list
description: Walks a chain of table entries, allocating a node for each and storing in it the result of a library lookup on the entry's value. The nodes are linked into a new list whose head is returned, or the list built so far when an allocation or lookup fails.

name: forbid_multitasking
description: Calls the Forbid routine of the exec library through the stored library base and returns, which stops task switching until a matching Permit call.

name: permit_multitasking
description: Calls the Permit routine of the exec library through the stored library base, re-enabling task switching after a matching Forbid call.

name: stamp_release_suffix_on_match
description: Checks that the buffer pointer is valid and that the byte at a fixed offset is the character two. If so, it compares a global string with the buffer text, and on a full match writes a dot and four spaces at a fixed offset; otherwise it advances the buffer while characters match the global string.

name: write_dot_and_four_spaces
description: Writes a dot followed by four space characters into a buffer at a fixed offset, filling five bytes. Nothing else is done.

name: advance_while_matching_global_prefix
description: Advances a buffer pointer for as long as its characters match a global string, stopping at the first mismatch or at the end of the global string.

name: return_without_action
description: Consists only of a return, with no computation or library call in its body. It does nothing when invoked.

name: call_exec_dispatch
description: Calls the Dispatch routine of the exec library through a stored library base and returns its result to the caller.

name: call_with_local_stack_slot
description: Forwards its two arguments to a second routine together with the address of a slot on its own stack, then returns.

name: calculate_string_length
description: Returns the number of characters before the terminator of a null-terminated string, by advancing to the terminator and subtracting the start address.

description: Stores its two arguments into global variables, then calls a routine with a fixed set of constants and global addresses. It finishes by calling a routine with the constant twenty.

name: run_file_pager_loop
description: Opens a window and runs an interactive loop over a file, showing a progress percentage and a quit prompt. It handles end-of-file, binary-content warnings and file-name prompts, with several exec library calls around the loop, and returns when the user quits.

name: iterate_table_with_function
description: Loops four times over a global table of values, calling a routine with each value and with a fixed field of the structure it is given.

name: validate_input_buffer
description: Calls a routine twice to fill or read an eighty-byte buffer, then scans its bytes. It returns zero when every byte falls within the accepted ranges and one at the first byte that does not.

name: dispatch_pager_key_command
description: Waits for an input signal with a timeout, then reads a key code and maps it to a pager action such as help, search or an escape-sequence key. Filtered codes are ignored, and a failed read sets the status to minus one before returning.

name: stub_unreached_gap_code
description: The recovered body is only a short call sequence ending in an indirect call, and it was reached only as a gap in the decode. The instructions may be data rather than a deliberate routine.

name: initialize_state_and_loop
description: Sets a counter to one and clears a flag in the structure, then calls a routine and stores its result. It conditionally calls another routine, then repeatedly calls a third while the counter is positive, the flag is clear and a pair of short fields is below its limit.

name: update_result_and_increment_counter
description: Calls a routine twice with arguments derived from the structure pointer and stores the second result in a field. When a flag field is zero it increments a short counter reached through a pointer stored in the structure.

name: scan_line_mark_form_feed
description: Fills a buffer through a routine, then scans it up to its length for a newline or form-feed character. A form-feed is replaced by a caret, the letter L and a newline, and a flag field is set, before the scanned length is returned.

name: run_display_loop_until_quit
description: Chooses a loop count from flags in the structure, and each pass calls a routine and forwards up to that many global values to another routine. After each pass it reads a character and stops when it is q or an interrupt character.

name: handle_search_loop
description: Selects a global string according to a flag in the argument block and runs a search over it, repeatedly calling a routine and counting down until the search reports a match. It returns one on a match and zero when the count runs out.

name: run_wrapped_call_with_cleanup
description: Runs a setup call, a call with the parameter block, an optional call that depends on a flag, then the main call, keeping its result. It finishes with two cleanup calls and returns the main call's result.

name: check_flag_and_call
description: Calls a routine with its first two arguments, then calls it again with the first argument only when a flag field in the structure is zero.

name: call_handler_pair_from_struct
description: Calls a routine with a stored value and a minus-one argument, then calls it again with a short field read through a pointer held in the structure.

name: call_handler_with_decremented_field
description: Calls a routine with a zero argument and the constant one, then calls it again with a short field read through a pointer held in the structure, minus one.

name: emit_text_lines_until_break
description: Clears a flag and counts the lines it outputs, limited by a field in the structure capped at 128 characters. It calls a routine to write each block, then scans backwards for newline and form-feed characters and stops when the line count is reached or a form-feed is found.

name: call_inner_then_dispatch_handler
description: Calls a routine with the structure pointer, then calls a handler stored in the structure with a global address and the first argument.

name: set_flag_and_forward
description: When a field in the structure is zero, it sets a short field in a linked structure to one. It then calls a routine with a stored handle and a global address, in both cases.

name: dispatch_by_flag
description: Chooses between a global address and a value read from a linked structure, depending on a flag in the block. It then calls a routine with the stored handle and both selected values.

name: dispatch_handler_by_flag
description: Calls a routine with a stored handle and a global address, followed by either two more global addresses or a short value read through a linked structure, depending on a flag in the block.

name: clamp_negative_result
description: Calls a routine twice with the same first argument and two different trailing values, then returns the second result with negative values replaced by zero.

name: consume_from_buffer
description: Takes up to the requested number of bytes from a buffer tracked inside the structure, first calling a refill routine when the request exceeds what is available. It advances the offset and read fields by the amount copied and reduces the remaining count.

name: reset_buffer_and_refill
description: Resets the buffer bookkeeping and calls a routine to fill the remainder of a 4096-byte block, adding the returned count to the remaining size when it is positive. If the block is not yet complete it returns zero, and otherwise it copies the offset fields and returns the call's result.

name: update_scroll_window
description: Computes a target offset from a mode argument and compares it with the current window bounds. When the target falls outside the bounds it resets the offset and size fields and calls a routine to move or redraw, otherwise it updates the position and remaining fields, and it returns the stored position or minus one for an invalid mode.

name: read_line_from_buffer
description: Reads bytes one at a time through a routine into a destination buffer, stopping after a newline or a fixed length limit, then appends a null terminator. It returns the number of bytes stored before the terminator.

name: copy_null_terminated_string
description: Copies bytes from a source to a destination until a null terminator has been copied.

name: convert_string_to_uppercase
description: Converts each lowercase ASCII letter in a null-terminated string to uppercase in place, leaving other bytes unchanged.

name: parse_signed_decimal
description: Parses a signed decimal integer from a null-terminated string, accepting an optional leading plus or minus sign. It accumulates digits until a non-digit and returns the negated value when a minus sign was seen.

name: call_handler_with_all_bits
description: When a pointer argument is non-null and a handle field in the structure is set, calls a routine with that handle, the pointer and an all-bits-set value. Otherwise it does nothing.

name: process_text_and_restore_state
description: Processes a text string by calling a routine with it, or with the structure when the string is empty, then restores several saved fields and, when a flag is set and the string is non-empty, reads characters until a line feed. It finishes by calling routines that re-enable the interrupt state.

name: build_message_buffer
description: Looks up a handle through a routine, places the argument in a one-word stack buffer, then passes that buffer with a constant tag and a length of one to a second routine. It returns the second call's result.

name: copy_fields_from_allocated_block
description: Allocates a 36-byte block and, if successful, passes it to a routine together with a constant. It copies two fields from the block into the caller's structure and releases the block, or returns zero when the allocation fails.

name: allocate_object_and_copy_words
description: Looks up a handle and allocates a 68-byte object, linking it to that handle and to a stored value. It copies the given number of words from a source address into the object and passes it to a routine, returning a field of the object, or zero when a step fails.

name: store_byte_at_address

name: divide_32bit_with_remainder
description: Divides a 32-bit value by a divisor, using a bit-by-bit shift-and-subtract loop for large divisors and two 16-bit divisions for small ones, and returns the remainder and quotient together as a pair of longwords.

name: multiply_32bit_partial_products
description: Computes the low 32 bits of the product of two 32-bit values from 16-bit partial products, returning that product in the high longword. The low longword holds the second operand with its two halves swapped.

name: stub_unreached_gap_code
description: The body is one call followed by a return, and it was reached only as a gap in the decode. It may be data decoded as code rather than a deliberate routine.

name: negate_on_flag
description: Calls a routine and keeps its first result, which is negated when the second result is non-zero. It returns that value.

name: call_rawdofmt_through_base
description: Calls the RawDoFmt routine of the exec library through the stored base and returns.

name: store_byte_at_address
description: Writes the low byte of a data register to the address held in an address register. Nothing else is done.

name: call_library_vector_276
description: Calls a library routine at a fixed offset through a stored base pointer taken from a global variable, with no arguments set up here, and returns.

name: allocate_signal_and_message

name: release_message_port_resources
description: If a link field is set, removes the block from its list, then marks its status fields as deleted. It frees the signal bit stored in the block with a library call and releases the 34-byte memory block.

name: search_substring_in_string
description: Returns one when the second string occurs in the first at any position, and zero otherwise. The search returns zero at once if the first string begins with a newline, and does nothing when the second string is empty.

name: setup_pointer_chain
description: Initialises a block as an empty linked list head, pointing its first word at itself plus four, clearing the following word and storing the block's own address in the third word.

description: Parses the DRIVE, NAME and option arguments, then checks that the drive exists and is empty and asks the user to insert a disk and press return. It handles the FFS and QUICK options, initialises the disk and creates its icons unless the NOICONS option is given, and returns an error code on failure.

name: release_format_buffers
description: Frees each stored buffer that is set. Two of them are released with fixed sizes of 260 and 36 bytes and the rest without a size, then the argument is passed on to a final routine.

name: report_disk_error_and_retry
description: Retries a disk operation while it returns a specific retry code, then maps the final error code to one of several messages such as bad sector, seek error, disk changed or cannot open device. It prints the chosen message and returns the mapped status.

name: return_status_after_message
description: Chooses between two sets of calls depending on a word argument, then passes a status byte to a further routine and returns it. It was reached only as a gap in the decode, so the instructions may be data rather than a deliberate routine.

name: match_value_in_table
description: Scans an eight-byte table in the global data for the given value and records the matching entry, or zero, in a field of a block obtained from a routine. It returns the argument unchanged.

name: find_drive_entry_in_list
description: Walks a linked list of drive entries, matching each either by name text or by a comparison routine. When it finds a match it calls two routines and returns one, and it returns zero when the list ends without a match.

name: calculate_string_length
description: Returns the number of bytes before the null terminator of a string.

name: copy_cstring_to_buffer
description: Copies a null-terminated byte string from a source pointer to a destination pointer, advancing both pointers and writing each byte up to and including the zero byte.

name: convert_character_to_uppercase
description: Returns the uppercase form of a single byte when it is a lowercase letter, otherwise returns the byte unchanged.

name: compare_strings_ignoring_case
description: Compares two null-terminated strings a character at a time, converting each character through a routine before comparing. It returns one when the strings match and zero at the first difference.

name: terminate_string_at_colon
description: Advances through a string to the first colon or terminator and overwrites the colon with a zero byte, truncating the string there.

name: store_arg_and_check_result
description: Stores its first argument in a one-word stack buffer and passes it with a constant and a length of one to a routine. It returns zero when that call succeeds and the constant one hundred twenty-six otherwise.

name: allocate_object_copy_capped_words
description: Looks up a handle and allocates a 68-byte object, linking it to that handle and to a stored value. It copies up to seven words from a source address into the object, passes it to a routine, and returns a field of the object, or zero when a step fails.

name: call_library_vector_354
description: Calls a library routine at a fixed offset through a stored base pointer taken from a global variable, with no arguments set up here, and returns.

name: call_alloc_mem
description: Calls the AllocMem routine of the exec library through the stored library base and returns its result to the caller.

name: call_alloc_signal
description: Calls the AllocSignal routine of the exec library through the stored base, with no arguments set up here.

name: call_library_vector_450
description: Calls a library routine at a fixed offset through the stored library base, with no arguments set up here, and returns its result.

name: close_library_base
description: Calls the CloseLibrary routine of the exec library through the stored base, releasing a library that was opened earlier.

name: call_library_vector_456
description: Calls a library routine at a fixed offset through the stored library base, with no arguments set up here, and returns its result.

name: call_find_task
description: Calls the FindTask routine of the exec library through the stored base and returns the task pointer it gives back.

name: call_free_mem
description: Calls the FreeMem routine of the exec library through the stored base, releasing a memory block.

name: call_free_signal
description: Calls the FreeSignal routine of the exec library through the stored base, with no arguments set up here.

name: call_get_msg
description: Calls the GetMsg routine of the exec library through the stored base and returns the message it gives back.

name: call_library_vector_444
description: Calls a library routine at a fixed offset through the stored library base, with no arguments set up here, and returns its result.

name: call_open_library
description: Calls the OpenLibrary routine of the exec library through the stored base and returns the library base it gives back.

name: call_library_vector_366
description: Calls a library routine at a fixed offset through the stored library base, with no arguments set up here, and returns its result.

name: call_library_vector_360
description: Calls a library routine at a fixed offset through the stored library base, with no arguments set up here, and returns its result.

name: call_library_vector_306
description: Calls a library routine at a fixed offset through the stored library base, with no arguments set up here, and returns its result.

name: call_wait_port
description: Calls the WaitPort routine of the exec library through the stored base and returns its result.

name: forward_stored_value_with_slot
description: Forwards a value held in a global variable together with its own argument and the address of a slot on its stack to a second routine, then returns.

name: call_library_vector_348
description: Calls a library routine at a fixed offset through a stored base pointer taken from a global variable, with no arguments set up here, and returns.

name: format_disk_tracks_with_progress
description: Allocates an interrupt server and track buffers, then formats the disk track by track, filling each buffer with DOS-style block headers, writing it out and verifying each track while printing a cylinder progress message. It removes the interrupt server, frees the buffers and returns a status code that reports disk port or cylinder errors.

name: run_device_command_sequence
description: Calls a device routine through a stored request block with the constants twenty and thirty, then with one, then forwards its argument together with a value from another routine. It returns nothing.

name: format_message_and_forward
description: Calls the RawDoFmt routine of the exec library through a stored base to format text into a 140-byte stack buffer. It then measures the formatted length and, if it is non-zero, passes the buffer and its length to a second routine.

name: store_byte_at_address
description: Writes the low byte of a data register to the address held in an address register. Nothing else is done.

name: divide_32bit_with_remainder
description: Divides a 32-bit value by a divisor using the same shift-and-subtract and 16-bit division paths as the other division routine, returning the remainder and quotient as a pair of longwords. It was reached only as a gap in the decode.

name: shift_subtract_divide_loop
description: Runs sixteen shift-and-subtract steps that shift a 32-bit dividend left one bit at a time and subtract the divisor from its high half whenever that half reaches it, setting a quotient bit. It was reached only as a gap in the decode and returns nothing.

name: multiply_32bit_partial_products
description: Computes the low 32 bits of the product of two 32-bit values from 16-bit partial products, returning that product in the high longword. The low longword holds the second operand with its two halves swapped.

name: call_rawdofmt_through_base
description: Calls the RawDoFmt routine of the exec library through the stored base and returns.

name: store_byte_at_address
description: Writes the low byte of a data register to the address held in an address register. Nothing else is done.

name: allocate_and_initialize_block
description: Allocates a signal bit and, if that succeeds, a 34-byte block whose fields are filled from the arguments, the signal number and a value from a routine. It passes the block on through one of two routines depending on the first argument, and returns the block, or zero when allocation fails.

name: release_message_port_resources
description: If a link field is set, removes the block from its list, then marks its status fields as deleted. It frees the signal bit stored in the block with a library call and releases the 34-byte memory block.

name: forward_with_constant_forty_eight
description: Passes its argument to a routine together with the constant forty-eight, then returns.

name: forward_argument_unchanged
description: Passes its single argument straight through to a second routine and returns.

name: init_trashcan_library_state
description: Stores a sentinel value in a field of a task-level structure while it looks up a value, then restores it and sets several global fields from fixed constants and the looked-up block. It calls a library routine that builds a function table and returns the status of a final lookup; the referenced text is a trashcan path.

name: extract_byte_from_call
description: Calls a routine to read one byte into a four-byte stack buffer. It returns that byte as a sign-extended value when the call reports exactly one byte, and minus one otherwise.

name: call_library_vector_240
description: Calls a library routine at a fixed offset through a stored base pointer taken from a global variable, with no arguments set up here, and returns.

name: setup_pointer_chain
description: Initialises a block as an empty linked list head, pointing its first word at itself plus four, clearing the following word and storing the block's own address in the third word.

name: store_size_and_pointer
description: If the pointer argument is non-null, allocates a block of the size given and, when that succeeds, stores the constant five in a byte, the size word and the pointer argument into fixed offsets. It returns the block, or zero otherwise.

name: reset_node_and_free
description: When the pointer is non-null, marks a byte and two longword fields as released with all-ones values, then passes the pointer and its stored size word to a routine and returns that result. A null pointer returns zero.

name: call_make_functions
description: Calls the MakeFunctions routine of the exec library through a stored base, with no arguments set up here.

name: call_init_struct
description: Calls the InitStruct routine of the exec library through a stored base, with no arguments set up here.

name: setup_task_and_parse_arguments
description: Allocates a task record and opens the dos library, then either fetches a stored handle or parses the command string into arguments, honouring quoted strings and star escapes for newline and escape characters. It calls a cleanup routine at the end and returns an error code when setup fails.

name: call_supervisor
description: Calls the Supervisor routine of the exec library through the stored base, with no arguments set up here.

name: call_exit_intr
description: Calls the ExitIntr routine of the exec library through the stored base, with no arguments set up here.

name: call_exec_switch
description: Calls the Switch routine of the exec library through the stored base, with no arguments set up here.

name: call_exec_dispatch
description: Calls the Dispatch routine of the exec library through a stored library base and returns its result to the caller.

name: call_make_functions
description: Calls the MakeFunctions routine of the exec library through a stored base, with no arguments set up here.

name: call_find_resident
description: Calls the FindResident routine of the exec library through a stored base pointer and returns its result.

name: call_enable
description: Calls the Enable routine of the exec library through the stored base, re-enabling interrupts, with no arguments set up here.
